newsitem.title: MEXICO: Grupo Mexico, others bid for Chihuahua-Pacific.
newsitem.headline: Grupo Mexico, others bid for Chihuahua-Pacific.

text.p: Grupo Mexico, Transportacion Maritima Mexicana (TMM) and Tribasa were authorized and registered as final participants in the bidding for the concession to run the Chihuahua-Pacific railroad, the Communications and Transport Ministry announced on Tuesday.
The ministry said in the official gazette that mining company Grupo Mexico was interested in the concession so as to transport mineral ores and finished products.

Grupo Mexico's ability to operate a railroad was backed up by a letter of intent from the South Orient Railroad Company Ltd, which operates three railroad lines in Texas between Dallas-Forth Worth and the border town Presidio. That would then connect with the Chihuahua-Pacific line.
TMM will participate in the bidding via Transportacin Ferroviaria Mexicana S. de R.L. de CV., a joint venture with Kansas City Southern Industries Inc.

"This group's particular interest...is explained by the intent to set up an important link in multi-modal transport systems for the partners involved, as a vehicle for making inroads in new markets in Latin America," the ministry said.

Tribasa vouched for its technical capacity by a letter of agreement with Impulsora Tlaxcalteca de Industrias, which makes railroad sleepers, and U.S.-based freight operators Railtex Service Company Inc.
Besides being an important industrial route, the line also includes a popular tourist venue through the spectacular Copper Canyon.
